root.title: Canonical problem
root.currentStateSummary: Three complementary converse directions are established. Genuine deterministic finite-block private-message codes induce approximate dependence balance, a fixed encoder-coordinate map, and four compatible rate rows, while an explicit nonbinary witness obstructs the specified coarse entropy and finite copy-lemma route; fixed-cardinality auxiliaries and exact BSSC posterior consistency remain unresolved. The separately relaxed UV scalars tensorize, with receiver-skew symmetry giving B_br=B_avg and half-skew BSSC product values n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4), but these scalars do not establish capacity. Conditional on the exact encoded Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9 premise, the private-message specialization is a 30-row system preserved by input-only product-marginal receiver replacement, yielding C_sum≤inf_{G,K}B(G,K). On any fixed N-point posterior grid containing {0,1/2,1}, receivers admit an exact at-most-N-output reduction; on Q0 the unrestricted and reflected finite-receiver infima both equal c=h_2(1/4)-1/2, and an explicit lower floor gives a necessary midpoint coercivity window below 2c. These new conclusions are confined to finite grids and establish no continuum cardinality, attainment, limit interchange, reflected full-functional optimality, capacity converse, or improved sum-capacity bound. For one specified exact-decimal binary receiver pair, a continuous weak-duality certificate conditionally gives C_sum≤0.369296945969202842443. The theorem premise and transcription remain unauthenticated, receiver and dual optimality and matching achievability are unknown, and the canonical capacity problem remains unresolved.
root.localResidualSummary: Authenticate or independently prove the full Theorem-9 premise, then bridge finite-grid receiver reduction to the continuum only through rigorous compactness, continuity, boundary, and limit arguments. Strengthen midpoint coercivity to global receiver control and determine whether the certified fixed pair is optimal. In parallel, derive exact binary-BSSC posterior and multiletter constraints for genuine code-induced laws and retain coupling or nested auxiliary structure absent from the additive relaxed UV scalars. Exact capacity still requires closing the converse gap and supplying a matching achievable rate.

program-bssc-structural-converse-refinem.title: Code-induced converse structure and BSSC-specific refinements
program-bssc-structural-converse-refinem.objective: Convert structure inherited from genuine private-message codes into certified BSSC converse bounds, while identifying which entropy relaxations are too coarse and which channel-specific constraints remain viable.
program-bssc-structural-converse-refinem.currentStateSummary: Every deterministic finite-block private-message code is known to induce an approximate dependence-balance relation, a fixed encoder-coordinate map, and four compatible rate rows. The auxiliary alphabets remain blocklength-dependent, preventing direct fixed-cardinality optimization. For the specified coarse BSSC entropy relaxation, a finite nonbinary entropic witness attains both direct-sum branches at 2h_2(1/4)-5/4 and survives all universal finite-variable information inequalities and every finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions. Thus that entropy/copy route is obstructed, but exact binary-posterior and other channel-specific consistency constraints remain available because the witness is not a binary-input BSSC law.
program-bssc-structural-converse-refinem.localResidualSummary: Prove a simultaneous support or compactness reduction preserving independence, time structure, the fixed encoder map, dependence balance, and all four rate rows; alternatively derive exact jointly consistent binary-BSSC posterior constraints or direct multiletter inequalities that exclude the witness and support a certified global converse optimization.

program-bssc-uv-scalar-tensorization.title: Tensorization of relaxed UV sum-rate scalars
program-bssc-uv-scalar-tensorization.objective: Characterize product behavior, symmetry reductions, and BSSC implications of the separately relaxed UV sum-rate scalar functionals, and determine which richer converse structures remain capable of multiletter improvement.
program-bssc-uv-scalar-tensorization.currentStateSummary: The averaged separately relaxed UV scalar B_avg is exactly additive for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBC products, even with correlated product-channel input laws and joint envelope auxiliaries. For receiver-skew channels with an involutive receiver-exchanging input symmetry, B_br equals B_avg, invariant input laws suffice, and finite products preserve the symmetry; consequently both scalars are additive on every finite product of such channels. Using the established global sharp BSSC posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving mixture, the half-skew BSSC satisfies B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) for every n≥1. The exact expression governs despite an inaccurate README decimal approximation. This exhausts blocking as a strengthening mechanism for these two separately relaxed scalar rows, but it does not address a common joint-(U,V) optimization, the full UV region, the GK functional, richer Theorem-9 systems, or capacity itself.
program-bssc-uv-scalar-tensorization.localResidualSummary: Investigate converse structures absent from the additive separately relaxed scalars, including coupling of UV branches through a common joint law, exact BSSC posterior consistency, nonsymmetric branchwise behavior, and richer GK or full-Theorem-9 auxiliary constraints. Any extension must be proved independently and connected to a certified capacity bound; the present scalar theorem itself moves no capacity endpoint.

program-bssc-theorem9-gk-foundations.title: Premise-bound Theorem-9/GK converse foundations
program-bssc-theorem9-gk-foundations.objective: Develop the full auxiliary-receiver Theorem-9 system into a rigorous private-message BSSC converse framework, separating premise authentication from conditional specialization, receiver reduction, and optimization of the resulting GK-type bound.
program-bssc-theorem9-gk-foundations.currentStateSummary: Conditional on the exact cited Theorem 9 outer-bound premise encoded in theorem9_spec.json, the private-message specialization is an independently generated 30-row system preserved by input-only product-marginal receiver replacement, yielding C_sum≤inf_{G,K}B(G,K), V_Q(G,K)≤V(1/2;G,K)≤B(G,K), and a finite V_0(g,k) on its realizable domain. For every fixed N-point posterior grid containing {0,1/2,1}, finite-output receivers can now be reduced exactly to at most N outputs while preserving V_Q; reflection-closed grids admit the analogous reflected support reduction. On Q0={0,1/2,1}, both finite-receiver infima equal c=h_2(1/4)-1/2, and the proved floor B(G,K)≥V_0(g,k)≥max{F(g),F(k)} gives an explicit necessary midpoint window for any pair with B(G,K)<2c. These are finite-grid and necessary-coercivity results only and provide no continuum cardinality, attainment, limit interchange, reflected full-functional optimality, or improved capacity bound. Separately, one specified exact-decimal binary receiver pair has an exact-rational six-row reduction and continuous directed-interval weak-duality certificate establishing the conditional bound C_sum≤0.369296945969202842443; receiver and dual optimality, achievability, exact capacity, and authentication of the external theorem remain unresolved.
program-bssc-theorem9-gk-foundations.localResidualSummary: Independently authenticate or re-prove the cited outer-bound premise and its quantifier structure. Extend the finite-grid reduction only with justified continuity, compactness, boundary control, or limit arguments capable of treating the continuum functional; determine whether the midpoint coercivity window can be strengthened to sufficient global receiver control. Optimize inf_{G,K}B(G,K), assess optimality of the certified fixed receiver pair and its dual face, and seek an appropriate matching achievable rate before drawing any exact-capacity conclusion.

result-code-induced-balance-entropy-copy.title: Code-induced dependence balance and entropy/copy obstruction
result-code-induced-balance-entropy-copy.statement: For independent uniform private messages A and B encoded deterministically over n uses of a finite-alphabet memoryless broadcast channel, with receiver errors p_1,p_2 and message alphabet sizes N_1,N_2 at least 2, let F_j=h_2(p_j)+p_j log_2(N_j-1), delta_j=F_j/n, and S_i=(Y^{i-1},Z_{i+1}^n). Then the exact telescope sum_i[I(A;B|S_i,Y_i)-I(A;B|S_i,Z_i)]=I(A;B|Y^n)-I(A;B|Z^n), together with separate Fano bounds on the endpoints, implies that the time-shared variables U=A, V=B, W=S_T, X=X_T satisfy |I(U;V|W,T,Y)-I(U;V|W,T,Z)| <= max{delta_1,delta_2}. Their law has the fixed-map factorization p(t,u,v,w,x,y,z)=(1/n)p_U(u)p_V(v)p(w|u,v,t)1{x=f_t(u,v)}P_{YZ|X}(y,z|x), and they satisfy the four compatible rows R_1<=I(U,W;Y|T)+delta_1, R_2<=I(V,W;Z|T)+delta_2, R_1+R_2<=I(U,W;Y|T)+I(X;Z|U,W,T)+delta_1+delta_2, and R_1+R_2<=I(V,W;Z|T)+I(X;Y|V,W,T)+delta_1+delta_2. For the specifically stated coarse uniform-input BSSC entropy relaxation—comprising the complete seven base entropies, message/time independence, deterministic encoding, fixed-map and memoryless Markov equalities, exact dependence balance, all stated conditional BEC identities, and the two sharp scalar posterior-support inequalities—an actual finite entropic witness attains both direct-sum branches at 2h_2(1/4)-5/4. Hence universally valid finite-variable information inequalities, including unknown non-Shannon inequalities, and any finite sequence of standard copy-lemma extensions cannot lower that relaxation below this value. The first conclusion is a sequence-level necessary condition, while the second is only a no-go theorem for the specified entropy/copy refinement route; neither is a BSSC capacity bound.
scopeQualifications: Exact binary-posterior and other channel-specific consistency constraints exclude or may exclude the witness and remain viable research directions.
The displayed Fano formula is literal for message alphabet sizes N_1,N_2 at least 2; singleton messages require a separate harmless convention.
The entropy witness is an actual finite distribution but is not an actual binary-input BSSC distribution: X is a tuple of six nondegenerate independent binary components.
The induced message and W alphabets may grow with blocklength, so the finite-block necessary condition is not by itself a fixed-cardinality single-letter outer region.
The no-go conclusion applies only to the specified coarse entropy, universal-information-inequality, and finite standard-copy-lemma relaxation.
The result supplies neither a broadcast-channel capacity bound nor an achievability result, capacity formula, or improvement of an existing certified numerical bound.

proofs: Each finite standard copy-lemma step remains feasible by conditional resampling of the finite witness while preserving the original marginal and objective.
Memorylessness and deterministic encoding give the fixed coordinate-map factorization, while conditioned Csiszar identities and nonnegative remainder terms give the four rate rows.
The dependence-balance identity is obtained by telescoping D_i=I(A;B|Y^i,Z_{i+1}^n), followed by separate Fano bounds at its two endpoints.

The no-go theorem is witnessed by an explicit finite distribution assembled from independent binary components whose component entropies verify the base entropy vector, structural equalities, dependence balance, all conditional BEC identities, both support rows, and both objective branches.
methods: Conditional-resampling realization of finite copy-lemma extensions
Finite-block information telescoping and time sharing
computations: An exact affine-in-h symbolic audit verifies positivity on 3/4<h_2(1/4)<7/8, the complete base entropy vector, structural equalities, both zero dependence-balance sides, all 65 disjoint-subtuple conditional BEC identities, both sharp support rows, and both objective branches at 2h_2(1/4)-5/4.
tools: The submitted Python standard-library checker performs the exact rational/affine symbolic witness audit without floating-point arithmetic.

result-uv-product-branchwise-additivity.title: Exact product and branchwise additivity of relaxed UV scalars
result-uv-product-branchwise-additivity.statement: For a finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channel W, let t_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)-I_p(X;Z), define A_W(p)=I_p(X;Y)+C[-t_W](p) and D_W(p)=I_p(X;Z)+C[t_W](p), where C is the upper concave envelope on the input simplex, and set B_avg(W)=sup_p(A_W(p)+D_W(p))/2 and B_br(W)=sup_p min{A_W(p),D_W(p)}. Then B_avg is exactly additive under arbitrary finite products of finite-alphabet discrete memoryless broadcast channels, including optimization over correlated product-channel input laws and envelope auxiliaries joint across factors. If a channel is receiver-skew, in the sense that an involutive input relabeling exchanges its receiver marginals up to output relabeling, then B_br(W)=B_avg(W), and the optimization may be restricted to invariant input laws. Finite products of receiver-skew channels preserve this property, so both scalar functionals are additive on every such finite product. For the half-skew BSSC P, the sharp one-letter posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving mixture supplied by result-code-induced-balance-entropy-copy-no-go give B_br(P^{×n})=B_avg(P^{×n})=n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) bits for every integer n≥1.
scopeQualifications: Exact additivity of B_avg holds for arbitrary finite-alphabet DMBC products, while equality B_br=B_avg and the resulting additivity of B_br require receiver-skew involutive symmetry and its finite-product closure.
The README decimal approximation is inaccurate; the exact expression n(2h_2(1/4)-5/4) is the established value and is unaffected.

The dependency result is needed only for the global sharp BSSC posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving posterior mixture used in the half-skew BSSC specialization; the general product and receiver-skew arguments are established analytically within this result.

The executable checker verifies selected numerical and algebraic identities, including the BSSC contact mixture and receiver-skew relations, but does not verify the global support inequality, concave-envelope optimization, or product theorem; those steps are discharged analytically.
The resulting separately relaxed BSSC scalar value supplies neither an achievability theorem nor a capacity formula or certified improvement of a governed capacity endpoint.

The theorem concerns only the two separately relaxed scalar UV functionals. It does not establish tensorization of the full UV region, optimization over a common joint (U,V), the GK functional, the full Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem-9 system, broadcast-channel capacity, or capacity tensorization.

proofs: Conditional mutual-information chain rules and cancellation of cross-factor co-information terms bound each product-channel concave-envelope contribution by the corresponding one-factor contributions; mutual-information subadditivity then gives the product upper bound for B_avg, while product priors and product posterior decompositions give the reverse inequality.

Coordinatewise receiver-skew involutions preserve the symmetry on finite products, and combining this closure with product additivity of B_avg proves finite-product additivity of both scalar functionals on the receiver-skew class.

For the half-skew BSSC, the dependency's global sharp posterior-support inequality and equality-achieving posterior mixture evaluate the one-letter envelopes at the invariant fair input law, yielding the exact value 2h_2(1/4)-5/4 per factor.

Receiver-exchanging involutive relabeling exchanges A_W and D_W. Concavity and symmetrization yield an invariant input law attaining at least the averaged value in the branchwise minimum, while min{a,d}≤(a+d)/2 gives the reverse bound.
methods: Conditional mutual-information chain rules and co-information cancellation
computations: The submitted standard-library script evaluates the half-skew BSSC identities at high precision and checks the contact posterior mixture and receiver-skew channel relations. These checks are corroborative and do not replace the analytic product, envelope, or global-support arguments.
tools: The submitted Python standard-library verifier checks selected algebraic and numerical specialization identities.

result-theorem9-private-message-product-.title: Conditional 30-row Theorem-9 specialization and product-marginal reduction
result-theorem9-private-message-product-.statement: Assume exactly the cited Gohari–Liu–Nair Theorem 9 outer-bound premise encoded in theorem9_spec.json: for each achievable rate triple there is one input prior that works for every finite auxiliary-receiver law, with an appropriate finite auxiliary hierarchy for each such law, under the encoded factorization, equations (19a)–(19p), and both side conditions. Conditional on that premise, setting R0=0, expanding every displayed minimum, and splitting the interval side conditions gives exactly the independently generated local 30-row private-message system. Every auxiliary-receiver information term in that system involves only G or only K, with no joint (G,K) term and no conditioning of one receiver output on another; consequently replacing G and K by their input-only product marginals preserves every row. Therefore, for the physical BSSC, C_sum ≤ inf B(G,K), where the infimum is over finite-output binary-input channels T_{G|X} and T_{K|X}. Under the submitted extended-real local definitions, including sup(empty set)=-infinity, V_Q(G,K) ≤ V(1/2;G,K) ≤ B(G,K). Moreover, every Q_0-supported row depends on the receiver channels only through (c,g,k,c), so V_0(g,k) is finite and well defined on the realizable (g,k)-domain.
scopeQualifications: Finiteness and well-definedness of V_0(g,k) hold only on the realizable (g,k)-domain.

The capacity conclusion is conditional on the premise's quantifier structure: one prior for each achievable rate pair works for every finite auxiliary-receiver law, with an appropriate finite hierarchy for each law.
The equality attestation establishes only syntactic and algebraic equality of the pinned encoded systems.
The product-marginal reduction relies on the audited system containing only single-output G or K information terms, with no joint (G,K) term and no conditioning of one receiver output on another.
The result does not authenticate the external theorem, manuscript, PDF, transcription provenance, rendering, or source fidelity.

proofs: An independently generated length-three path construction agrees row by row with the encoded 30-row specialization after only the stated mutual-information chain-rule normalizations.
Expanding the minima in the encoded equations after imposing R0=0 produces 26 scalar rows, and splitting the two interval side conditions produces four further nonnegative-slack rows.

Posterior mutual-information identities for Q_0-supported hierarchies reduce every row to the four midpoint channel values (c,g,k,c); explicit feasible zero rates and binary-output entropy bounds establish finiteness on the realizable domain.

The exhaustive output-term audit shows that all G- and K-bearing terms are single-output marginals. The factorization then preserves every relevant marginal when the auxiliary receiver is replaced by the product of its input-only G and K marginals.
methods: Exact symbolic expansion of minima and interval conditions
Independent path-row generation and algebraic normalization
computations: The submitted standard-library verifier checks the encoded factorization, all sixteen equation labels and two side conditions, generates all 30 private-message rows independently, compares their rate coefficients and signed information terms exactly, and audits the distinct output-bearing terms.

The premise-bound six private-message inequalities, an exact-rational nonnegative dual combination, and directed-interval majorization over the full continuous posterior domain establish C_sum ≤ U for a certified value U in [0.36929694596920284244271335135600317726937686320586339865039784778686683932875798, 0.36929694596920284244271335135600317726937686320586339865039784778686683932875818], and hence C_sum ≤ 0.369296945969202842443. result-finite-grid-q0-cardinality-coerci.title: Finite-grid receiver reduction and exact Q0 coercivity
result-finite-grid-q0-cardinality-coerci.statement: Using the accepted private-message 30-row definitions and optimization order supplied by result-theorem9-private-message-product-marginal-foundation, let Q be an N-point posterior grid containing {0,1/2,1}. Every finite-output binary-input receiver has an at-most-N-output replacement with identical mutual-information samples on Q. Consequently, inf over finite-output G,K of V_Q(G,K) equals the infimum restricted to |G|,|K|≤N; when Q is reflection closed, the infimum of V_Q(m,m^circ) over finite m equals its restriction to posterior measures with support size at most N. For Q0={0,1/2,1} and c=h_2(1/4)-1/2, both the unrestricted finite-receiver and reflected finite-receiver infima equal c. Moreover, every finite-output input-only pair G,K with g=J_G(1/2) and k=J_K(1/2) satisfies B(G,K)≥V_0(g,k)≥max{F(g),F(k)}, where F(x)=2c·max{c,x}/(c+x). Hence, as a necessary condition, c≤U<2c and B(G,K)≤U imply 2c^2/U-c≤g,k≤Uc/(2c-U).
scopeQualifications: No continuum cardinality theorem, attainment claim, limit interchange, capacity-converse interpretation, or improved sum-capacity bound is established.

The declared dependency is required for the accepted 30-row definitions, optimization order, single-output term structure, and inequality V_Q(G,K)≤B(G,K); external manuscript authenticity is not required.
The midpoint window is necessary only and supplies no sufficient condition or off-midpoint control for the full receiver functional.
The reflected-class conclusion is proved only for reflection-closed finite grids; no full-functional reflected-optimality assertion is established.
The result is limited to finite posterior grids and finite-output receivers.

proofs: Combining B(G,K)≥V_0(g,k) with the two branches of F and solving F(g),F(k)≤U yields the stated necessary midpoint interval.

Representing a binary-input receiver by its fair-prior posterior measure expresses every sampled channel curve value as an integral. Carathéodory's theorem applied to the mean and the N-2 nonendpoint samples gives an exact representing measure with at most N atoms.

The complete Q0 hierarchy parametrization and the H, L, and X witness families establish V_0(g,k)≥max{F(g),F(k)} across all midpoint regimes. A reflection-invariant three-output revealing-erasure receiver has sampled curve (0,c,0) and attains c, proving both Q0 infimum equalities.

The dependency's exhaustive single-output term structure and posterior mutual-information identities show that matching the sampled receiver curves preserves every row, feasible set, and objective of the Q-supported hierarchy. For reflection-closed Q, applying the reduction before reflection preserves the reflected receiver class.
